name: English Wikipedia, articles naming a writing register
totalDerivedFrom: no fixed list: the leaf layer is not enumerable from a catalogue, so a row is written for each article read while looking up the manner named under a live broad cell, from 2026-09-09

terms.note: movement: ordinary life reported without heightening, from mid-nineteenth-century French and Russian literature; minted as the parent Dirty realism and Kitchen sink realism both needed. Proposal B10 #14. Written and attested 2026-09-09.

manner: the essay addressed to one reader, about the writer and a subject at once, with Lamb as the standing example. The article has no page of its own and names the form in its own section; the cell carries that as a question. Proposal B10 #15. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: the essay built by image and juxtaposition, named by Tall and D'Agata in the Seneca Review in 1997. Proposal B10 #16. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
form: a signed 500-to-700-word argument from outside the publication, fixed by the New York Times page opposite the editorials. Proposal B10 #17. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: reporting written with the devices of fiction; the working register of long-form nonfiction and the parent New Journalism needed. Proposal B10 #18. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
movement: the American narrative reporting of the 1960s and 1970s, named by Wolfe and Johnson's 1973 anthology. Proposal B10 #19. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: first-person reporting with the writer as protagonist, named for Thompson's 1970 Kentucky Derby piece. Proposal B10 #20. Written and attested 2026-09-09.

manner: reporting organised around the background a news item assumes; a Pulitzer category since 1985 and the register most long-form blog posts and topic newsletters use. Proposal B10 #21. Written and attested 2026-09-09.

tradition: observation of the natural world kept together with the observer, from Gilbert White through Thoreau, Leopold and Carson; three live writing styles credit it. Proposal B10 #22. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
form: a reader's question and a named columnist's answer, continuous since the Athenian Mercury in 1690. Proposal B10 #23. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
form: rolling timestamped coverage of an event as it happens, standard in news since the mid-2000s. Proposal B10 #24. Written and attested 2026-09-09.

register: writing meant to be understood on one reading, with a shelf of guidance from Gowers in 1948 to the United States federal guidelines; the live Plainhand style credits it. Proposal B10 #25. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: documentation in short task-oriented pieces, set out by John Carroll and carried into the DITA standard. Proposal B10 #26. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
form: the Unix manual page, terse and declarative in a fixed sequence of sections, with fifty years of work by many hands. Proposal B10 #27. Written and attested 2026-09-09.

form: the compressed standalone claim, from La Rochefoucauld through Lichtenberg and Nietzsche; recorded on the Microblogs cell as the nearest named register for the short post. Proposal B10 #28. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: the clipped, dialogue-heavy crime register of the American pulps under Prohibition, with Hammett and Chandler as the standing names. Proposal B10 #29. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
movement: the Gothic relocated to the American South, where the haunting is social history; Faulkner, O'Connor, McCullers and Welty. Proposal B10 #30. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: horror that invents its own uncategorisable monsters, around Hodgson, M. R. James, Clark Ashton Smith and Lovecraft. Proposal B10 #31. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
movement: weird fiction from the 1990s on, named by M. John Harrison in 2002; Mieville, VanderMeer, Swainston, Bishop. Proposal B10 #32. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
movement: speculative fiction of a future where the climate problem was solved, from 2008 on. Proposal B10 #33. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: the chronicle register of the self-consistent invented world, with the conventions Tolkien fixed. Proposal B10 #34. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: fast episodic fantasy of personal danger, from Howard's Conan stories, with the name in use since the early 1960s. Proposal B10 #35. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: dystopian, amoral and violent speculative fiction from the 2000s on, named from the Warhammer 40,000 tagline. Proposal B10 #36. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
manner: fiction from the author's own life published as fiction, with the author's name on the narrator; Doubrovsky coined the word in 1977. Proposal B10 #37. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
movement: spare North American fiction of unglamorous life, named by Bill Buford in Granta in 1983; Carver, Wolff, Ford, Beattie. Proposal B10 #38. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
movement: British working-class writing of the late 1950s and early 1960s, with regional speech on the page. Proposal B10 #39. Written and attested 2026-09-09.

manner: the long contemporary novel of absurd plotting over careful social reporting, named by James Wood in 2000; the cell records that the name began as a complaint. Proposal B10 #40. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
register: sustained denunciation of a society's morals ending in a prophecy of ruin, with a continuous American line from the Puritan sermon. Proposal B10 #42. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
